title: Phase 4: spike graph clustering for component discovery (L1)
description:
Layer 1 (architecture/components) depends on graph clustering (Louvain/Leiden) which hasn't been validated yet. Spike it on real codebases.

Experiments:
- Run Louvain/Leiden on sutra's existing call/dependency graph
- Evaluate: do the clusters map to recognizable subsystems?
- Test stability: how much do clusters change when a few files change?
- Compare cluster quality at method, class, and file granularity
- Test blending with HRR structural similarity (0.7 graph / 0.3 HRR)
- Measure: component count vs codebase size

Test codebases: sutra itself, chitta, a larger project

Done criteria:
- Clusters on at least 2 real codebases
- >60% of clusters map to recognizable subsystems (manual eval)
- Stability assessment across simulated edits
- Blend with HRR evaluated
- Verdict: viable / viable with caveats / not viable
decisions: Louvain viable for L1 component discovery at file granularity
HRR blending via all-pairs edges not viable — adds too much noise (91K edges vs 2316 original on linux/kernel). Restrict to reweighting existing graph edges.
Function-level clustering too granular for L1 — use file-level
1/ambiguity weighting essential for name-based call graph construction
execution_record:
Ran Louvain community detection on call graphs extracted via tree-sitter across 3 codebases:

| Codebase | Files | Clusters | Q | Purity | Stability | HRR Blend |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| sutra | 57 | 7 | 0.2975 | 74.7% | NMI 0.860 | -10.7pp |
| redox-kernel | 183 | 34 | 0.1977 | 67.9% | NMI 0.791 | +2.4pp |
| linux/kernel | 491 | 92 | 0.5509 | 88.0% | NMI 0.911 | -7.2pp |

All done criteria met:
- Clusters on 3 real codebases (>= 2 required)
- >60% purity on all 3 (74.7%, 67.9%, 88.0%)
- Stability: all stable (NMI > 0.79 at 10% removal)
- HRR blend: evaluated, hurts in 2/3 cases
- Verdict: VIABLE for file-level L1 component discovery

Key findings:
1. File-level Louvain works well. Modularity increases with codebase size.
2. Function-level too granular for L1 (7390 clusters for 18K functions on linux).
3. HRR blending as implemented (adding all-pairs edges) hurts — adds too many noise edges. Should restrict to reweighting existing call edges only.
4. 1/ambiguity weighting for name resolution is important for cross-file call graph quality.
5. Single-level Louvain sufficient (no multi-level needed for tested sizes)."
